name: Harlen Broad-Port Utility Trouser
description: A straight-leg utility trouser in dark charcoal twill with a wide tail port — reinforced with a double-layer gusset and a hook-and-eye closure that widens to 8cm base diameter, accommodating thick or bushy tails. The waistband is cut lower at the back to reduce pressure on the tail base. Side cargo pockets. Honest, unfussy workwear for people with geneware that standard tail ports can't handle.
functionality: Wide-gauge tail port (up to 8cm base diameter) with hook-and-eye sizing adjustment; lowered rear waistband reduces tail base pressure
what_it_says: You've got a large tail and you've been fighting ill-fitting clothes long enough to find the one brand that actually sized the port correctly.
worn_by: people who've ruined too many pairs of pants
story_hooks: The brand only sells in two shops in Tier 2 — both owned by the same person, who has a large tail themselves and started the label out of frustration.
A character is given a pair of these as a gift from someone who clearly paid attention to what they struggled with daily.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System

physical_description.visual_profile: Straight-leg utility trouser with a distinctly modified silhouette—tailored for non-human morphology. The back waistband sits noticeably lower than standard pants, creating an asymmetrical profile when worn. A prominent, reinforced tail port dominates the rear, engineered for function over fashion. Overall impression is deliberately utilitarian, built for bodies that reject corporate standardization.
physical_description.fit: Straight leg with a comfortable but deliberate fit through the hip and thigh. The waistband is cut lower at the back (approximately 2-3cm below standard) to reduce compression on the base of the tail. The port area features extra fabric architecture to accommodate thick or bushy tails without binding. Side seams sit straight and true.
physical_description.primary_material: Dark charcoal twill—durable, practical, with a subtle weave texture. The gusset reinforcement uses a heavier ballistic-grade twill to withstand repeated flexing and pressure.
physical_description.texture: Twill weave with visible diagonal ribs; slightly rough to the touch, broken-in but not soft. The double-layer gusset creates a subtle ridge of doubled fabric around the port opening. No sheen—matte finish typical of working-grade synthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Solid dark charcoal gray, almost black in low light. No patterns or accent colors—pure utilitarian palette. Stitching in dark matching thread is visible but not decorative.
physical_description.closures: Hook-and-eye closure system at the tail port that expands to 8cm diameter base—oversized to accommodate larger tail roots. Likely a standard waistband zipper or friction-fit closer at the front.
distinctive_features: Reinforced double-layer gusset around tail port opening
Wide hook-and-eye port closure (8cm diameter) for non-standard geneware
Lower-cut back waistband to reduce tail-base pressure
Side cargo pockets with reinforced stitching
No branding or aesthetic flourish—purely functional design
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional workwear. Affordable, honest engineering for working-class augmentation users. Not cheap, but not aspirational—prices itself at honest utility value.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by gene-modded workers, tail-ported individuals, and anyone whose augmentations fall outside corpo-standard clothing infrastructure. Signals honest living, non-conformity to baseline human design, and pragmatism over vanity. Street cred among the augmented underclass.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually worn broken-in—light creasing at the knees, minor fraying at pocket edges, possible stress marks around the port from regular use. Patina of honest work, not damage. Typical wearer maintains it carefully; it's a necessity, not a disposable fast-fashion item.

The hook-and-eye port closure is visible and in focus. Moody blue-gray neon ambient lighting reflecting off the twill weave.
